decision.explanation: The basis vectors are orthogonal: a₁·a₂=0. Thus the closest vector is the projection (x·a₁)/(a₁·a₁)a₁+(x·a₂)/(a₂·a₂)a₂. Since x·a₁=24, a₁·a₁=12, and x·a₂=0, this equals 2a₁=[4,4,4]ᵀ.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the vector in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ 
that is closest to the vector $x,$ where 

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly independent. 

The closest vector to $x$ in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace, which is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}12 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}24 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{12} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}24 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace
content.problem:
Find the vector in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ 
that is closest to the vector $x,$ where 

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly independent. 

The closest vector to $x$ in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace, which is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}12 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}24 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{12} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}24 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $x$ onto the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & \text{ }1\,\, &  \\ 1 & \text{ }1\,\, \\ 0 & \,\,\,-1\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & \text{ }1\,\, &  \\ 1 & \text{ }1\,\, \\ 0 & \,\,\,-1\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & \text{ }1\,\, &  \\ 1 & \text{ }1\,\, \\ 0 & \,\,\,-1\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & \text{ }1\,\, &  \\ 1 & \text{ }1\,\, \\ 0 & \,\,\,-1\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & \,\,-1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & \,\,-1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
content.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $x$ onto the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & \text{ }1\,\, &  \\ 1 & \text{ }1\,\, \\ 0 & \,\,\,-1\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & \text{ }1\,\, &  \\ 1 & \text{ }1\,\, \\ 0 & \,\,\,-1\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & \text{ }1\,\, &  \\ 1 & \text{ }1\,\, \\ 0 & \,\,\,-1\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & \text{ }1\,\, &  \\ 1 & \text{ }1\,\, \\ 0 & \,\,\,-1\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & \,\,-1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & \,\,-1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $x$ onto the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}12 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of the vector x onto the plane r=sv+tw, where s,t∈R, and v=[10−1],w=[11−2],x=[6−63].

EXPLANATION

First, notice that v and w are linearly independent.

The orthogonal projection of x onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix A is given by projSx=A(ATA)−1ATx.

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace S=Span{v,w} in R3. In our case, we have A=[||vw||]=[1101−1−2]⟹AT=[10−111−2].

Therefore, we get the following projection:

projSx=[1101−1−2]⋅([10−111−2]⋅[1101−1−2])−1⋅[10−111−2]⋅[6−63]=[1101−1−2]⋅[2336]−1⋅[3−6]=[1101−1−2]⋅13[6−3−32]⋅[3−6]=[1101−1−2]⋅[12−7]=[5−72]

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
content.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $x$ onto the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}12 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Find the vector in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ 
that is closest to the vector $x,$ where 

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly independent. 

The closest vector to $x$ in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace, which is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}11 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}11 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find the vector in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ 
that is closest to the vector $x,$ where 

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly independent. 

The closest vector to $x$ in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace, which is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}11 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}11 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $x$ onto the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
